players.note: Isaiah Likely has been crushing it as the TE6 in fantasy points per game. Likely has an 81.1% route share, a 30.4% target share, 1.84 YPRR, six red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 34.1% first-read share. He has been amazing. He should have another outstanding week against a defense that has allowed the third-most yards per target and the most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Harold Fannin is the TE8 in fantasy points per game with at least 10.4 PPR points in each of his last three games. Fannin has a 78.4% route share with a 20% target share, 1.40 YPRR, three red zone targets, one deep target, and a 16.3% first-read share. Temper your expectations for Fannin this week. The Jets have limited tight ends to the 11th-fewest yards per target and the seventh-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Juwan Johnson has been a steady fantasy producer with at least 10.8 PPR points in each game as the TE4 in fantasy points per game. Johnson has a 14.4% target share with 1.69 YPRR, seven red zone targets (WOW!), one deep target, and an 18.7% first-read share. The Vikings have faced the eighth-fewest tight end targets this season, but they have surrendered the tenth-highest yards per target to the position. Johnson should flirt with strong TE1 production again this week.

Well, this looked like what we thought we were getting in 2026 with Colston Loveland last week. While he didn't post a massive stat line, Loveland had a 66.7% route share and 91% snap share as he led the team with a 26.5% target share and 34.8% first-read share. Loveland had three red zone targets, 57 receiving yards, and 2.38 YPRR. This week, Loveland faces a Green Bay secondary that has the sixth-highest two-high rate in the NFL (62.1%). Over the last two weeks, against two high, Loveland has had an elite 35% target-per-route run rate and a strong 1.88 YPRR. Green Bay is 16th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to tight ends. The last time Loveland faced the Packers, he secured eight of his 15 targets with 137 receiving yards. I'm not saying that he'll post that type of stat line, but he could easily lead the team in targets again this week with Bagent slinging it around the yard.

TJ Hockenson is the TE11 in fantasy points per game. Hockenson has a 22.7% target share with 2.14 YPRR, four red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 23.5% first-read share. All of his per-route numbers and fantasy production are being inflated by his massive outing in Week 4, but he was also the TE9 in weekly scoring in Week 1 with Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison active. Hockenson could easily be the number two target in the Minny passing attack this week with a wonderful matchup and return TE1 production. New Orleans has allowed the fifth-most yards per target and the 12th-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Mark Andrews is the TE18 in fantasy points per game, but he finally finished as a TE1 last week (TE8). His per-route data has been awesome, though. Yes, among 46 qualifying tight ends, he ranks 16th in route share (67.5%), but also in that same sample he is fourth in target share (22.9%), 12th in YPRR (1.80), and fifth in first-read share (26%). Andrews has three red zone targets and one deep target. Andrews could easily be a TE1 again this week. Atlanta is 14th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to tight ends, while surrendering 15.6 PPR points to Pat Freiermuth, 18.3 PPR points to Darren Waller, and 11.9 PPR points to Juwan Johnson this season. Those three tight ends combined for three scores, and Johnson could have easily had a score at the end of the game last week, but the target went to Devaughn Vele.

Mike Gesicki is the TE13 in fantasy points per game with at least 12.7 PPR points in three of four games. He could see an elevated role this week with the state of the Cincy depth chart and injuries. If we take out his dude in Week 2, Gesicki has scored a touchdown in every other game. Excluding the stinker in Week 2, Gesicki has had a 54.8% route share, an 11.9% target share, a 20% target-per-route run rate, 2.09 YPRR, and a 12.6% first-read share. He has three red zone targets and two deep targets. Gesicki should shred the Miami secondary this week. The Dolphins have allowed the most yards per target and the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

With Mason Taylor back this week, Kenyon Sadiq is likely tossed right back into a frustrating tight end committee situation. In Weeks 1-2, with Taylor active, Sadiq had only a 39.3% snap share, 41.3% route share, and 7.7% target share. Maybe he sees more work this week than that with Adonai Mitchell still sidelined, but it's not a certainty. The Browns are 15th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to tight ends while also giving up the 13th-fewest yards per target to the position. Sadiq is a must-sit this week with a middle-of-the-road matchup and questionable usage for Week 5.

Hunter Henry is the TE29 in fantasy points per game. His best finish in weekly scoring was last week as the TE16 in fantasy. Since Week 2, Henry has had a 12.2% target share with 1.47 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and a 17.3% first-read share. Henry is a viable streaming option this week. Vegas has been allowing a ton of production to tight ends, giving up the fifth-most receiving fantasy points per game and the second-most receiving touchdowns (tied) to the position.

Jake Ferguson is the TE22 in fantasy points per game with only one huge game this season. Ferguson has only one outing with more than ten PPR points this season. Ferguson has only a 10% target share with 0.76 YPRR, four red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 9.6% first-read share. Outside of his touchdown equity in this Dallas passing attack, he has been a forgotten player. Maybe that changes this week, but I'm not holding my breath. The matchup is nice for Ferguson, so he's on the streaming radar. He's a touchdown-or-bust option, though. Tampa Bay has allowed the ninth-most yards per target and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Dalton Schultz has seen his route share decline weekly. In Week 1, he was rocking a 73.8% route share, but last week he was down to 60%. Does it make any sense? Nope, but hey, it's the Texans, and none of their player usage makes any sense. Schultz has an 18.4% target share with 1.83 YPRR, two red zone targets, three deep targets, and a 19.4% first-read share. He has been the consistent WR2 for the offense despite his declining playing time. Schultz is a viable streaming tight end option. Tennessee's season-long stats are good against tight ends, but they haven't really been tested with injuries and bad quarterback play until last week. Mark Andrews and Matthew Hibner secured seven of their eight targets last week with 61 receiving yards and a score. Schultz could produce low-end TE1 numbers in Week 5.

Brenton Strange is the TE21 in fantasy points per game after finishing as the TE5 in weekly scoring last week. Strange has a 17.3% target share with 2.04 YPRR, two red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 19% first-read share. I expect this to be a quieter week for Strange against a defense that has allowed the 12th-fewest yards per target and the sixth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Pat Freiermuth is the TE18 in fantasy points per game with two outings this season with 10.7 PPR points or more. Freiermuth has a 63.2% route share, which has dipped below 60% in two of his four games. That's not great. Freiermuth has a 12.3% target share with 1.16 YPRR, three red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 12.2% first-read share. Freiermuth is only a low-end streaming option this week. Indy is 18th in fantasy points per opportunity allowed to tight ends. He's a touchdown-or-bust option.

Last week, in Jalon Daniels first start, Cade Otton led the team with a 28.6% first-read share while also logging a 22.2% target share (second on the team). Otton was only the TE24 for the week despite the strong usage. He finished with 37 receiving yards, 1.42 YPRR, and zero red zone and deep targets. If Otton sees this type of market share in Week 5, he'll be a strong streaming option. Dallas has allowed the eighth-most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. We have seen random big games from Otton in the past, and that could happen again this week.
Dallas Goedert is back at practice. He opened this week (knee) with a limited practice. I'll update his outlook on Friday. It's possible that he could return this week.

With Brock Bowers back in the lineup over the last two games, Michael Mayer has been the TE13 and TE7 in weekly scoring. During that short span, Mayer has had a 14.1% target share, 1.70 YPRR, one red zone target, zero deep targets, and a 12.2% first-read share. Mayer isn't on my streaming radar this week against a defense that has held tight ends to the sixth-fewest yards per target and the second-fewest fantasy points per opportunity.

Kyle Pitts is the TE51 in fantasy points per game, and that's after coming off his best game of the season, which isn't saying much. Pitts has seen below a 50% route share in two of four games this season (38.1% last week) while failing to eclipse a 15% target share or 17% first-read share in any game. With this type of minuscule usage, it's impossible to plug him into a fantasy lineup.
